name: Chemical Engineering
boundaries: Chemical Engineering: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.reason: Covered by CHE-04 for bulk close-boiling and isomer separations, and by CHE-09 for carbon dioxide from air. Not added. “Zero-energy” and simultaneous perfection for every mixture conflict with the minimum work of unmixing. The 10–15% energy figure is the Georgia Tech description of Sholl and Lively, already used in CHE-04, not a new result.

original_dispositions.original_title: Inherently safe runaway-proof reactor for any chemistry
original_dispositions.reason: Inherent safety is an existing design practice. Kletz framed it as “the avoidance of hazards rather than their control by added-on protective equipment,” after Flixborough, using minimization, substitution, moderation, and simplification (quoted in Murphy and Ackroyd, The Chemical Engineer, https://www.thechemicalengineer.com/features/flixborough-50-years-on-application-of-inherent-safety-principles-to-plant-design/; IChemE Loss Prevention Bulletin 297, June 2024, https://www.icheme.org/media/26776/lpb297_pg13.pdf). A 2012 AIChE CEP article records his 1978 lecture “What You Don’t Have, Can’t Leak” and states that eliminating every hazard is not always feasible (https://www.aiche.org/sites/default/files/cep/20120140-1.pdf). A geometry or material that makes thermal runaway physically impossible for every exothermic chemistry and every scale would have to erase inventory and heat release themselves. That is not a missing scientific principle of the same kind as the calibration examples. Smaller inventory and wider operating limits are applications of the principle already in use.
Covered by CHE-05. Not added as a second entry. The “less than 5% deviation” test is not in Duduković and Mills or in the 2025 fluidized-bed study.

original_dispositions.original_title: Ambient electrochemical platform for all commodity chemicals
original_dispositions.reason: Covered in pieces by CHE-01 (ammonia), CHE-03 (olefins and liquid fuels), and only partially by CHE-02 and CHE-06. Not added. One modular device with greater than 90% Faradaic efficiency for ammonia, ethylene, methanol, aromatics, and polymers at once bundles several unsolved reactions and treats their success as a single discovery. Aromatics and polymers are further breakthroughs even if ethylene electrolysis succeeds.

original_dispositions.original_title: Perfect heat integration with 100% recovery and no added capital
original_dispositions.reason: Pinch analysis already supplies the minimum hot and cold utilities for a chosen minimum approach temperature. Linnhoff and Hindmarsh’s design method is the standard statement of that result (described in the A to Z of Thermodynamics process-integration entry, https://doi.org/10.1615/atoz.p.process_integration). A standard treatment of the composite curves states that a zero temperature difference “would require an infinitely large heat exchanger” (chapter extract of Pinch Analysis and Process Integration, https://www.shahroodut.ac.ir/fa/download.php?id=1111129792). One hundred percent heat recovery for every plant, including transients, with no extra area, is not an open discovery. It contradicts the second-law trade-off the method was built to expose. Typical utility savings from applying the existing method are large and incremental relative to this bar.

Model-predictive control and real-time optimization are deployed industrial tools. Nature Chemical Engineering’s 2025 focus treats robotics and self-driving laboratories as a live research front for discovery and some processing, not as an absent principle that would create lights-out plants of every scale (journal index for the May 2025 focus, https://www.nature.com/natchemeng/articles?searchType=journalSearch&sort=PubDate&year=2025&page=7). Removing operator error worldwide would still depend on sensors, maintenance, and abnormal-situation chemistry that no control architecture has been shown to close. That is an automation program, not a new capability at the calibration scale.

Tunable and switchable solvent families already exist and still fall short of dissolving any solute and returning forever with zero loss. The direct consequence would be cleaner fine-chemical and pharmaceutical processing. Extending that to “any reaction previously impossible” inflates the claim. It does not clear the bar next to CHE-04 or CHE-10, and a universal solvent is not required for those entries to stand.

original_dispositions.original_title: One device that reacts, separates, and manages heat so every equilibrium-limited reaction goes to completion in one pass
original_dispositions.reason: The principle is already commercial for specific chemistries. Agreda, Partin, and Heise described Eastman’s reactive-distillation process for high-purity methyl acetate (Chemical Engineering Progress 86, no. 2, 40–46, 1990; bibliographic record, https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/High-purity-methyl-acetate-via-reactive-Agreda-Partin/901c70d6f67d44f1608645e4f6d8140ee7136401). A 2025 AIChE abstract dates large-scale Eastman production to 1984 (Omota, https://proceedings.aiche.org/conferences/aiche-spring-meeting-and-global-congress-process-safety/2025/proceeding-444). Extending reactive distillation or membrane reactors to every equilibrium-limited reaction is valuable process intensification. Where the product must be protected from further reaction, the open case that still meets the revolutionary bar is CHE-02, not a second general device class. Near-100% conversion of every such reaction in one pass is a broader claim than the demonstrated methyl acetate plant.

original_dispositions.original_title: A systems theory that recycles 100% of atoms for all chemicals
original_dispositions.reason: Not added. The material flow large enough to stand alone is mixed plastic waste, already CHE-07. Designing every process so nothing is ever downcycled or lost is an umbrella goal. It counts downstream successes in ammonia, CO2 chemistry, solvents, and separations as if they were one discovery.

original_dispositions.original_title: A bioreactor with ideal oxygen and shear from 1 L to 1,000,000 L for any cell
original_dispositions.reason: Not added. Large fermenters and large mammalian-cell reactors already operate. Remaining gradients are a scale-up problem inside CHE-05. Making fuels and chemicals cheaper than petrochemical routes also requires titer, yield, and feedstock cost. Those are further biological and process breakthroughs, not a direct result of removing gradients.

reconciliation_change_log.change: CHE-01 through CHE-10 are unchanged in identity and ID. No concept was deleted, replaced, or merged.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: None of the ten historical items becomes a new concept. No eleventh concept met the revolutionary-impact bar.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Significance text now flags where a historical item overlaps without absorbing it.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Completion criteria were not relaxed to match the historical numbers.

reconciliation_change_log.change: CHE-04 is narrowed in words only. Zero-energy separation of every mixture is identified as thermodynamically overstated. CHE-09 remains the dilute-air case.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The plant-scale close-boiling capability is the same concept as before.

reconciliation_change_log.change: The historical “less than 5% deviation” figure is rejected as an invented threshold.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The proposed demonstration is still a first commercial multiphase reactor that meets its design point without a pilot plant.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Current state now includes Bi et al., Nature Chemical Engineering, 14 October 2025, yields up to 79% ethylene plus propylene from polyethylene without external hydrogen or olefins, at laboratory mass.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: That narrows the co-feed gap and leaves mixed waste, cost, and tonne-scale operation open. Conk et al. 2024 remains the post-consumer polyolefin result that uses ethylene as a co-reactant.

reconciliation_change_log.change: No new ID was assigned. Fossil-parity electrolysis, calcination-free cement, seawater ions, and first-principles catalyst design were reconsidered under the cost-and-scale clause.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Commercial electrolysis already exists and is largely limited by electricity price and manufacturing; cement chemistries have reached pilot certification; seawater extraction and universal catalyst design do not yet show a consequence at the calibration scale beyond problems already listed.
